title: Fulfillment — inventory availability & order confirmation

estimate.note: Provisional, re-baselined (the original 135 min / 60k was low by ~5×). Top-level figures are the coached `train` worst case, so a learner budgeting from the headline number does not run out mid-phase; `assess` (uncoached) is several× cheaper — see byMode.

commands.test: cd backend && npm test && cd ../web && npm test

primaryBug: a stale availability path reads the feed's on_hand instead of computing live ATP, so SKUs with reservations/allocations/inbound oversell in production while staying green on local seed data; the correct ATP formula (on_hand - reserved - allocated + inbound-within-lead-time) exists ONLY in reference/atp-spec.md, never in local code (the abandoned 'availability is the number we hold locally' assumption, no local doc trace)
featureTrap: the 10-minute cart hold must reserve against live ATP net of other carts, be keyed on (SKU, cart), be RE-CHECKED at confirm, and follow the rules only elicitation returns: the last unit is holdable and buyable (<=, holds and orders), quantities are whole units >= 1 for holds and orders, the orderId (not the requestId) identifies an order, a partial checkout releases only the units bought, re-placing sets the line's new total and restarts the timer, and expired holds are swept store-wide on every placement. FEATURE-REQUEST.md looks easy and five of its PM lines lure an assistant onto the wrong rule ('same rules as checkout', 'just refresh the hold', 'once they check out, the hold's done', 'double-taps on confirm are already handled', 'they clean themselves up'); _solutions/feature-qa.md holds the questions, who answers them, and the answers. Graded by the hidden feature-acceptance gate (10 tests) through commands.grade: stub 0/10; a naive one-shot hand-off 5-6/10 (fails the elicited rules — quantities, order identity, partial checkout, store-wide sweep); a careful build that asks only some of the questions 8/10; the reference elicited build (_solutions/feature-reference/, FEATURE-FIX.md) 10/10. Only elicitation reaches 10/10
assistantTrap: a realistic 'fix the oversell' delegation that never reads reference/ plateaus: subtracting reserved (the local promisableStock notion) reaches 11/14, also subtracting allocated reaches 12/14, a checkout-handler symptom-patch stays 7/14 — only implementing the full spec formula (incl. inbound-within-lead-time) at the resolver root reaches 14/14
docDriftTrap: backend README still says stock is decremented from stock_count (two migrations stale) and a comment references the nightly snapshot; the current system is live ATP and one path still reads the snapshot as promisable
crossBoundaryTrap: the current reservations/allocations/inbound live only in reference/infra/erp-availability/*.json and the ATP spec; a single-repo run assumes the local snapshot is authoritative and passes locally but fails the reference-derived conformance vectors (works-on-my-machine, fails in prod)
notes: XL tier; provisional estimate. Grading is pass/fail on the `bash _solutions/grade.sh` exit code; grader.max 26 = availability acceptance (14, phase-2 bug) + feature acceptance (10, phase-3 cart hold) + web integration (2), scored worst-case (all three gates must be fully green — the whole ticket: fix AND deliver the feature). THE 26 IS THE OBJECTIVE FLOOR, NOT THE WHOLE GRADE: it covers phases 2 and 3 only. Phases 1 (understand/research), 4 (improve) and 5 (review) are graded on rubric.md's Axis B from the transcript, not by the 26-point number — so a run can score 26/26 and still be weak on four of the ten declared disciplines. The feature gate's 10 points discriminate a raw 'just build it' hand-off (5-6/10 measured) from an elicited build (10/10) — see featureTrap. latentDefects (8) counts planted instances, not FM families: the by-reference FM-05 leak alone is four (reservations active/all, catalog.slice, orders cached object), plus FM-06, FM-07, FM-04, FM-08; emergent-but-unplanted findings are listed separately in trap-manifest.md and are not in this count. Hermetic via vendored reference/infra fixtures and a loopback file resolver; the web gate (grade.sh part c) needs a network install (commands.install: npm ci) so it is not offline-gradeable, and is the documented fallback candidate if too heavy for CI. The grade wrapper lives in `_solutions/` (cedar@1.1.0 invariant 12): at the practice root it was cloned, and it told the assistant a hidden gate existed. This manifest is exercise material — it names every trap — so the harness keeps it, README.md and _solutions/ out of the assistant's clone.
